sentences.text: The airport-level constraint process starts by translating en-route demand indicators into rates, time windows, and advisories that can be understood by local operations teams.
Each Sector Load Monitor supplies time-bucketed counts, predicted occupancy, and overload flags for the sectors that feed or constrain Meridian arrivals and departures.
The Regional Flow Platform aligns these sector values with scheduled movements from Flight Data Exchange and predicted readiness from Demand Prediction Service.
When a sector is predicted to exceed its planning threshold, Capacity Assessment Module evaluates whether the affected traffic is dominated by departures, arrivals, or mixed flows.
For departure-dominated overload, the conversion result is normally an airport departure rate, a constrained departure fix allocation, or a proposed spacing value at the runway release point.
For arrival-dominated overload, the result is expressed as an adjusted Airport Acceptance Rate or a metered arrival stream for Arrival Regulation Console.
Mixed-flow constraints are converted into paired measures so that departure metering does not protect one sector by creating an unmanaged arrival queue.
The Regional Flow Manager uses the load sheet to confirm whether a departure fix constraint should be represented as an airport departure measure.
Departure fix saturation is calculated by comparing planned departures by fix against the usable fix capacity declared in Airport Capacity Plan.
Capacity Assessment Module applies Business Rules Registry thresholds to distinguish a short tactical peak from sustained saturation requiring a Tactical Regulation Proposal.
A short peak normally becomes a sequence advisory in Tower Sequence Manager or a limited departure metering adjustment in Departure Metering Service.
Sustained saturation is converted into revised Calculated Takeoff Time targets and, when necessary, adjusted Target Off Block Time values published through Airport CDM Portal.
The Slot Allocation Engine preserves equity by distributing delay across operators according to the active Ground Delay Program logic and local priority rules.
The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews the airport-level result to determine whether flight swaps, cancellations, or recovery plans are needed inside the airline schedule.
The Tower Supervisor uses the same result to understand whether a runway queue is being held for surface capacity, runway capacity, or downstream airspace capacity.
The Surface Surveillance Adapter produces the Runway Lighting Outage Card when monitored runway lighting status affects a declared operating configuration.
En-route constraints received from network coordination are normalized into constraint records with an affected route, start time, end time, expected capacity, and confidence value.
The Airspace Sector Planner validates the operational meaning of each constraint before it is allowed to influence airport rates.
The Military Airspace Liaison confirms whether conditional route availability changes the effective capacity before the constraint is converted to a local measure.
Weather-related en-route limitations are correlated with information from Weather Ingest Gateway so that airport measures reflect both sector capacity and route availability.
In Normal Operations, the conversion may only produce monitoring alerts because sector demand remains below the action threshold.
In Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State, the same inputs are allowed to produce binding metering values, revised rates, and additional coordination tasks.
All converted measures are displayed on Common Situation Display with the source constraint, effective interval, affected runway or fix, and expected delay impact.
Alert Distribution Hub sends notifications to Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, and Network Operations Liaison when a measure changes operational behavior.
Collaborative Decision Log records the constraint, chosen conversion rule, responsible actor, and time of approval for traceability.
Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares predicted sector pressure, actual airborne delay, and airport departure compliance to tune Demand Prediction Service and Capacity Assessment Module.
